newsitem.title: CROATIA: Rijeka port confirms proposed S.Korean loan.
newsitem.headline: Rijeka port confirms proposed S.Korean loan.

text.p: Croatian Rijeka port on Wednesday confirmed it hoped to use a $34.5 million loan from Samsung Corp for upgrading old technology, so as to catch up with main competitors in Slovenia and Italy.

"Our cranes are 30 years old and technologicaly incapable of meeting the market's demands. This would make us competitive with the ports of Koper and Trieste," director Bojan Hlaca told Reuters by telephone.
He said the loan, negotiated on a government level between Croatia and South Korea, would probably be concluded in a year.
Samsung's Zagreb office said the deal was in progress, but could not release any further details of the company's plans.
Rijeka has lost 36 percent of its traffic this year. But with the help of new investment its annual capacity could increase to 10 from the pressent three million tonnes of goods.
Due to its importance as the key seaport with good rail and road links with the interior, Hlaca said the government had granted it a special status which should help its development.

It guaranteed a 15 million German mark foreign loan two months ago to bail it out of old debts and has also opened a tender for companies to operate a free zone there. -- Metka Jelenc, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
